acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Parties got married in 2001. Two girls were born from their wedlock. Appellant claimed respondent was treated with respect but later cancelled honeymoon due to sudden illness of his Nanaji.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's refusal to have physical relationship with the other is a significant factor in determining the state of their marriage.
legal_principles.held: Faced with such conduct, they both approached a marriage counsellor in the year 2010 and also on 24.04.2015 and 31.01.2016, but the respondent did not follow the advise of the counsellor.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's failure to follow the advice of a marriage counsellor can be considered in determining the state of their marriage.
legal_principles.held: They both approached a marriage counsellor in the year 2010 and also on 24.04.2015 and 31.01.2016, but the respondent did not follow the advise of the counsellor.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's refusal to discuss matrimonial discord and patch up differences for the sake of children can be considered in determining the state of their marriage.
legal_principles.held: When he tried to discuss the matrimonial discord with the respondent, she retorted that she do not even want to see his face. All his request to patch up the differences for the sake of children, went unheeded by the respondent.

outcome.final_order: Trial court's decision dismissing divorce petition upheld by the High Court.
